summary: Flathead County, MT L-4 cab on the Flathead NF dated 1929; lookout Harold Hatton was struck by lightning in July 1937; listed gone.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says abandoned and gone, with no date; the FFLA Montana list also marks it gone.

events.note: Firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1929
Harold Hatton was the Forest Service lookout at Pagoda Mountain in July 1937

On July 13 lightning struck Hatton and a companion while they repaired a telephone line near the lookout. The companion is Roy Root in the Northern Region News report and the Forest Service history, and J. Wirth in the July 15 Billings Gazette report. Hatton never regained consciousness and died at a hospital; Root recovered per the news report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Northern Region News report and the Forest Service history name Roy Root as the companion; the July 15 Billings Gazette report, reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page, names J. Wirth, who it says felt no ill effects. The story reports both names.
A 1937 newspaper reprint gives a 12-mile horseback ride from the lookout to the Black Bear landing field; the Forest Service history gives 11 miles. The story reports both.
One 1937 newspaper reprint calls the lookout Leonard Harold Hatton; the Forest Service history and other reprints use Harold Hatton. The story uses Harold Hatton.

notes_for_editor: Record status gone and kind ground are supported (firelookout L-4 cab; FFLA Ground Gone). The 1937 lightning strike is not a fire; it is recorded as event other and staffing as staffed 1937. The newspaper quotes are as printed on the Forest Lookouts page; they were not checked against scans. Firelookout.com gives no date for abandonment, so there is no abandoned event. Searches: two.
